skill.name: lark-workflow-standup-report
skill.description: Create Lark standup reports by combining calendar agenda and incomplete task data for a chosen date.
skill.summary: Combines Lark calendar events and pending tasks into a clear daily or weekly standup summary.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command names, fixed Lark CLI examples, relative documentation links, and multilingual text entropy. No evidence found of hidden execution, arbitrary filesystem traversal, prompt injection, obfuscation, or data exfiltration intent in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The skill asks users to run Lark CLI commands that access calendar and task data.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing explicit authorization step and document that results may contain personal work information.

remediation.issue: Relative links to shared Lark skill documentation can trigger path traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep links scoped to known sibling skill files and avoid user-supplied path parameters.

content.value_statement: Daily planning is slow when meetings and tasks live in separate Lark apps. This skill combines calendar agenda and unfinished tasks into one standup-ready summary.
actual_capabilities: Guides authentication for Lark calendar and task scopes.
Fetches calendar agenda data for today or a specified date range.
Fetches incomplete Lark tasks with optional due date filtering.
Formats meetings and tasks into a standup-style report.
Maps RSVP status values into readable status labels.
Identifies schedule conflicts and estimates free time from agenda data.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and authorized by the user.
Supports user identity only, not tenant-wide administrative reports.
Date ranges must use ISO 8601 or Unix timestamp formats.
Summary quality depends on the completeness of returned Lark data.

use_cases.title: Prepare a personal standup
use_cases.description: Review today’s meetings, pending tasks, conflicts, and open time before the workday starts.

use_cases.title: Plan tomorrow’s priorities
use_cases.description: Generate a next-day agenda and task view before ending the current day.

use_cases.title: Check weekly workload
use_cases.description: Review upcoming schedule pressure and unfinished tasks for a short planning window.

prompt_templates.title: Today’s simple report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create my Lark standup report for today. Include meetings, incomplete tasks, conflicts, and free time.

prompt_templates.title: Tomorrow’s planning report
prompt_templates.prompt: Create my Lark standup report for tomorrow. Use the correct ISO date range and include tasks due by tomorrow.

prompt_templates.title: Focused task and meeting review
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize my Lark schedule and unfinished tasks for this date. Highlight overdue tasks and meetings that need RSVP action.

prompt_templates.title: Weekly workload scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a Lark workload report for this week. Group events by day, list incomplete tasks by due date, and call out schedule conflicts.

output_examples.input: Create my standup report for today.
output_examples.output: A dated report with a meeting table, incomplete task list, conflict reminders, and a short daily summary.

output_examples.input: Show tomorrow’s agenda and tasks due by tomorrow.
output_examples.output: A next-day planning summary with calendar events, pending tasks, overdue markers, and estimated free time.

output_examples.input: Review my week for conflicts and unfinished work.
output_examples.output: A weekly overview that groups schedule items by day and highlights unresolved task load.

best_practices: Authorize only the calendar and task scopes required for the report.
Use ISO 8601 date ranges for any day other than today.
Filter tasks by due date when you need a concise standup report.
anti_patterns: Do not omit the incomplete-task filter for pending task summaries.
Do not use natural language date strings in Lark CLI date arguments.
Do not treat declined meetings as busy time when checking conflicts.

faq.question: What does this skill summarize?
faq.answer: It summarizes Lark calendar events and incomplete Lark tasks for a chosen day or planning window.

faq.question: Does it need Lark authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. The user must authorize lark-cli with calendar and task permissions before using the workflow.

faq.question: Can it use natural language dates?
faq.answer: No. The workflow says date arguments must use ISO 8601 values or Unix timestamps.

faq.question: Does it include completed tasks?
faq.answer: No. The workflow instructs the assistant to request incomplete tasks with the complete=false filter.

faq.question: Can it detect meeting conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares sorted event start and end times and reports overlapping meetings.

faq.question: Is it for team-wide reporting?
faq.answer: No. The skill states it supports user identity only, so it is intended for personal reports.
